baseDailyCasualtyRate.note: Pre-state/early warfare; scaled from Krentz hoplite data below at 0.8x for less lethal stone/copper weapons. Educated guess. Krentz: https://grbs.library.duke.edu/article/viewFile/5321/5325
As tech 0-2: Krentz-based ancient rate x0.8. Educated guess. https://grbs.library.duke.edu/article/viewFile/5321/5325
Krentz-based ancient rate x0.9. Educated guess. https://grbs.library.duke.edu/article/viewFile/5321/5325

Krentz 1985 (hoplite battles): victors lost avg ~5% killed (typical 3-10%), vanquished avg ~14% (10-20%), killed only. Pre-rout rate at 1:1 ~ victor's 5% killed x2 for wounded = 0.10; high = geometric mean of totals sqrt(0.10 x 0.28) = 0.17.
No systematic medieval series; kept at the Krentz-based ancient value (rates before 1600 were not lower per Dupuy's trend). Range as tech 3.

Dupuy, Attrition Fig. 13 'Average daily battle casualty rates 1600-1973' (losers/winners, read off the chart, reproduced at this URL): Thirty Years War losers ~30%/day, winners ~20%/day. 1:1 base between winner and loser; pursuit losses are added separately, so mid 0.20 sits at the winners' rate.

Dupuy, Attrition Fig. 13 'Average daily battle casualty rates 1600-1973' (losers/winners, read off the chart, reproduced at this URL): Napoleonic losers ~21%/day, winners ~15%/day; French Revolution ~16/9.5. Mid 0.16 ~ geometric mean sqrt(21 x 15) = 17.7 minus pursuit share.

Dupuy, Attrition Fig. 13 'Average daily battle casualty rates 1600-1973' (losers/winners, read off the chart, reproduced at this URL): c.1900 losers ~12-13%/day, winners ~8%/day; WWI ~10/7. Bodart: Franco-German War 1870-71 average 7.5% bloody losses per battle (quoted in https://www.generalstaff.org/BBOW/LOV-DUP/ADA298124_CAA-RP-95-1.pdf).

Dupuy, Attrition Fig. 13 'Average daily battle casualty rates 1600-1973' (losers/winners, read off the chart, reproduced at this URL): WWII losers 3.3%/day, winners 2.3%/day. QJM standard rates: attacker 2.8%, defender 1.5% per day for divisions (https://dupuyinstitute.org/2019/12/26/how-attrition-is-calculated-in-the-qjm-vs-the-tndm/). Mid 0.025.

Dupuy, Attrition Fig. 13 'Average daily battle casualty rates 1600-1973' (losers/winners, read off the chart, reproduced at this URL): 1973 October War losers ~3.1%/day, winners ~2.1%/day; low allows the continuing decline (CAA: casualty fractions declined 1600-present, https://www.generalstaff.org/BBOW/LOV-DUP/ADA298124_CAA-RP-95-1.pdf).
Extrapolated: 1973 value 0.022 x 0.8 for continued dispersion; high 0.03 because drone/artillery-heavy fighting in Ukraine 2022-26 kept rates near WWII levels. Educated guess.

powerRatioExponent.note: CAA-RP-95-1 (Helmbold 1995), finding n/p: fractional exchange ratio favouring the defender FERY ~ 0.5 x FRY^0.6, favouring the winner FERW ~ 7.4 x FRW^0.5, with battle date having very little influence. Engine: loss_loser/loss_winner = R^(2 alpha), so 2 alpha = 0.5-0.6 -> alpha 0.25-0.30. Note the CAA exponents are on numerical force ratio, the engine applies alpha to power ratio. Pre-1600 data are thinner (CAA set starts 1600); high 0.45 allows the more decisive ancient/medieval outcomes (Krentz winner:loser killed ratios 1:2 to 1:5).

defensePostureFactor.note: QJM posture factors (NPW Table 5, p.230): hasty defense 1.3, prepared 1.5, fortified 1.6, attack 1.0.

fortificationFactor.note: Palisade: about a QJM hasty-defense factor 1.3 (https://dupuyinstitute.org/2022/08/16/the-defensive-value-of-urban-terrain-according-to-the-qjm/). Educated guess.
Mudbrick walls: between QJM fortified 1.6 and stone walls. Educated guess.
Ashlar city walls with towers; garrisons routinely held against several-fold superior attackers until starved or stormed. Educated guess.
Concentric castles: the peak of pre-gunpowder fortification; small garrisons held against large armies. Educated guess.
Trace italienne bastioned fortress. Educated guess.
Concrete ring forts; Liege 1914 fell in days to super-heavy siege guns. Educated guess.
QJM posture factor 'fortified defense' 1.6 (NPW Table 5, p.230, quoted by TDI); fortified city adds urban terrain (QJM urban 1.4, applied separately), so mid 1.8.
QJM fortified 1.6 as floor; hardened shelters. Mid 1.8.
Layered air defence, but precision strike reduces fixed-fortification value; kept at tech-9 value. Educated guess.

surpriseFactor.note: TNDM multiplier for complete surprise is 2.5, degraded by historical period; partial surprise is lower. Mid 1.8.

pursuitLossFraction.note: Interpreted as extra loss fraction of a routed force when the pursuer is fully mobile (engine scales by the winner's mounted/mobile share). Krentz: hoplite losers lost ~14% killed vs ~5% for winners, most of the gap in flight (https://grbs.library.duke.edu/article/viewFile/5321/5325). Educated guess.

Interpreted as extra loss fraction of a routed force when the pursuer is fully mobile (engine scales by the winner's mounted/mobile share). Krentz: hoplite losers lost ~14% killed vs ~5% for winners, most of the gap in flight (https://grbs.library.duke.edu/article/viewFile/5321/5325). Educated guess.

Interpreted as extra loss fraction of a routed force when the pursuer is fully mobile (engine scales by the winner's mounted/mobile share). Krentz: hoplite losers lost ~14% killed vs ~5% for winners, most of the gap in flight (https://grbs.library.duke.edu/article/viewFile/5321/5325). Educated guess.

Ancient pursuit: Krentz hoplite losers ~14% vs winners ~5% killed with little cavalry (https://grbs.library.duke.edu/article/viewFile/5321/5325); with mounted pursuers losses run much higher: Carrhae 20,000 killed + 10,000 captured of 42,000 vs 10,000 horse (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Carrhae). Engine scales by mounted share.

Medieval: Agincourt French ~6,000 killed + 700-2,200 captured, much of it after the line broke (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Agincourt). Engine scales by mounted share. Educated guess on the magnitude.

Pike-and-shot: Dupuy's 1600s loser-winner gap ~10 points/day (https://dupuyinstitute.org/2016/11/12/what-is-the-relationship-between-rate-of-fire-and-military-effectiveness/, Attrition Fig. 13) is mostly pursuit. Educated guess.

Napoleonic loser-winner gap ~6 points/day (https://dupuyinstitute.org/2016/11/12/what-is-the-relationship-between-rate-of-fire-and-military-effectiveness/, Attrition Fig. 13); Jena-Auerstedt Prussian 41,000 losses incl. captured vs French 12,600 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Jena–Auerstedt). Educated guess.

Trench-era firepower made pursuit costly; loser-winner gap ~4 points/day (https://dupuyinstitute.org/2016/11/12/what-is-the-relationship-between-rate-of-fire-and-military-effectiveness/). Educated guess.
Mechanized pursuit and encirclement: Bagration German losses 399,102 of which 262,929 missing/captured (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Bagration). Engine scales by mobile share.
Mechanized pursuit under air power. Educated guess.
Drone ISR makes pursuit and withdrawal both costly. Educated guess.

captureFraction.note: Pre-state warfare: few prisoners kept. Educated guess.
Early states took captives as labour/slaves. Educated guess.
Cannae Roman losses: Polybius 70,000 killed / 10,000 captured (12.5%), Livy 48,200 / 19,300 (29%) - ancient figures; Carrhae 10,000 of 30,000 (33%, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Carrhae).
Interpolated between medieval (0.2) and Napoleonic (0.3-0.56). Educated guess.
Austerlitz Allies: 15,000-16,000 killed/wounded + 12,000-20,000 captured -> 43-56%; Waterloo French 25,000 K/W + 8,000 captured -> 24% (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Waterloo). Mid 0.35.
Trench-war battles had low prisoner shares, mobile 1914 battles high. Educated guess.
Bagration German losses (Frieser): 399,102 incl. 262,929 missing/captured -> 66%; encirclement battles typical of the era; mid 0.5.
Late Cold War conventional wars (1973, 1991 Iraq) had high prisoner shares for collapsing forces. Educated guess.
Drone-era attritional warfare: few large surrenders. Educated guess.

water.note: Attacking across water = amphibious: TNDM multiplier 2.00 for amphibious attack across a beach (attacker casualties), so attacker power ~1/2.

plains.note: Attacker factor = 1/ru. HERO, Opposed Rates of Advance of Large Forces in Europe (ORALFORE), 1972, App. E Table 2 "Terrain factors (r)" p. App-E10 (fetched, page image read): defense-position factor ru (attacker always 1.0) rugged heavily wooded 1.5, rugged mixed 1.55, rugged bare 1.45, rolling heavily wooded 1.35, rolling mixed 1.45, rolling bare 1.3, flat heavily wooded 1.1, flat mixed 1.2, flat bare 1.05; tanks rwi 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 0.7, 0.9, 1.0; mobility rm 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 0.7, 0.9, 1.0. The 1985 QJM (Numbers, Predictions and War, Table 1 p.228, quoted by TDI, fetched: https://dupuyinstitute.org/2022/08/16/the-defensive-value-of-urban-terrain-according-to-the-qjm/) gives rugged-mixed 1.5, rolling-mixed 1.3, urban 1.4, so the table was revised between versions. Plains = flat bare: 1/1.05 = 0.95. High 1.0 = no terrain effect (the QJM attacker baseline). Out-of-sample check, CDB90 (https://github.com/jrnold/CDB90, 573 battles with terrain and strengths after removing every battle of a backtest war): logistic fit of attacker win on ln(force ratio) plus terrain class gives terrain coefficients all within 1 SE of zero (attackers choose where to attack), so CDB90 neither confirms nor refutes these factors and sets none of them. Was 0.9/1.0/1.0 C.

App-E10 (fetched, page image read): defense-position factor ru (attacker always 1.0) rugged heavily wooded 1.5, rugged mixed 1.55, rugged bare 1.45, rolling heavily wooded 1.35, rolling mixed 1.45, rolling bare 1.3, flat heavily wooded 1.1, flat mixed 1.2, flat bare 1.05; tanks rwi 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 0.7, 0.9, 1.0; mobility rm 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 0.7, 0.9, 1.0. The 1985 QJM (Numbers, Predictions and War, Table 1 p.228, quoted by TDI, fetched: https://dupuyinstitute.org/2022/08/16/the-defensive-value-of-urban-terrain-according-to-the-qjm/) gives rugged-mixed 1.5, rolling-mixed 1.3, urban 1.4, so the table was revised between versions. The QJM column is for WWII-era armour; applying it to horse cavalry is an assumption. Forest between rolling heavily wooded 0.6 and flat heavily wooded 0.7, mid 0.65. Was 0.3/0.5/0.7 D.

desert.note: Proxy (derived:qjm-terrain-proxy): no fetched rwi row, so rwi is taken equal to the QJM 1985 mobility factor rm (Clark 1989, https://archive.org/details/dimensionalnalys1094526997, Fig. 42 p.63, fetched: flat desert 0.95, "rolling dunes" 0.3, swamp-jungle 0.3, swamp mixed or open 0.4, urban 0.7). ice.note: Multiplier on mounted and vehicle roles' power by terrain. QJM gives separate terrain effects for mobility (https://dupuyinstitute.org/2022/08/16/the-defensive-value-of-urban-terrain-according-to-the-qjm/ quotes only the defensive column); values here are educated guesses consistent with restricted/severely restricted going. Snow and ice. No QJM row for snow/ice terrain in any fetched table (ORALFORE 1972, Clark 1989); left grade D.

riverCrossingFactor.note: TNDM has an amphibious/river-crossing factor; amphibious across a beach is 2.00. A contested major river is taken as 1/1.67 (between beach 1/2 and a minor stream ~0.8). Educated interpolation.

combinedArmsBonus.note: Bonus = combinedArmsBonus x doctrine.combinedArms x roleDiversity. No quantitative source found; Dupuy lists combined arms among the adaptations to lethality (https://dupuyinstitute.org/2016/11/12/what-is-the-relationship-between-rate-of-fire-and-military-effectiveness/). Educated guess.

battleHoursPerDay.note: Rounds per battle day. Battle durations have increased over time (CAA finding a); pre-modern battles lasted a few hours, modern combat runs in day and night phases. Mid 10.

qualityFactor.note: Converts a 0..1 rating to a multiplier (low at 0, mid at 0.5, high at 1). Calibration: Dupuy's CEV - TNDM caps the opponent CEV at 1.5 (https://dupuyinstitute.org/2019/12/26/how-attrition-is-calculated-in-the-qjm-vs-the-tndm/); Israeli forces won 81% of attacks at odds below 1:1 while Arab forces lost every attack below 3.94:1 (https://dupuyinstitute.org/2019/11/28/force-ratios-in-the-arab-israeli-wars-1956-1973/), implying a combined effectiveness gap of ~2-3x spread over quality, training, command and morale. Equipment quality within an era (TLI handles the tech level), so the narrowest of the three.

trainingFactor.note: Converts a 0..1 rating to a multiplier (low at 0, mid at 0.5, high at 1). Calibration: Dupuy's CEV - TNDM caps the opponent CEV at 1.5 (https://dupuyinstitute.org/2019/12/26/how-attrition-is-calculated-in-the-qjm-vs-the-tndm/); Israeli forces won 81% of attacks at odds below 1:1 while Arab forces lost every attack below 3.94:1 (https://dupuyinstitute.org/2019/11/28/force-ratios-in-the-arab-israeli-wars-1956-1973/), implying a combined effectiveness gap of ~2-3x spread over quality, training, command and morale.

cohesionBreakpointShift.note: Breakpoint += shift x (cohesion - 0.5): an elite unit (cohesion 1.0) breaks ~10 points later, e.g. 0.30 -> 0.40, matching the FM 105-5 defender breakpoint of ~40% (https://dupuyinstitute.org/2024/03/26/the-40-rule/). Educated guess.

phalanxFront.note: Frontal multiplier for a deep pike/spear phalanx; comparable to a hasty-to-prepared defensive gain (QJM 1.3-1.5, https://dupuyinstitute.org/2022/08/16/the-defensive-value-of-urban-terrain-according-to-the-qjm/). Educated guess.

phalanxFlank.note: Phalanx struck in flank/rear or broken ground (Cynoscephalae, Pydna); ancient loss reports are lopsided. Educated guess.

horseArcheryOpening.note: Horse archers' opening rounds against slower melee forces; Carrhae: 42,000 Romans lost 30,000 to 10,000 Parthian horse (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Carrhae). Educated guess on the multiplier.

feignedRetreatPursuerLoss.note: Loss multiplier for pursuers caught by a feigned retreat; ENGINE.md specifies one round at 2x. Educated guess.

fieldFortification.note: Nightly fortified camp = QJM hasty defense 1.3 (prepared 1.5) per NPW Table 5.

massedArtillery.note: Massed artillery doctrine; artillery caused 40-50% of casualties before 1850 and 71% in WWI (Attrition Figs. 19 and 35, https://dupuyinstitute.org/2016/11/12/what-is-the-relationship-between-rate-of-fire-and-military-effectiveness/). Educated guess on the multiplier.

defenseInDepth.note: Defense in depth: between hasty 1.3 and prepared 1.5 relative to attack (QJM, https://dupuyinstitute.org/2022/08/16/the-defensive-value-of-urban-terrain-according-to-the-qjm/), applied on top of posture. Educated guess.

humanWavePower.note: Power multiplier for massed infantry assaults. Educated guess.

humanWaveOwnLoss.note: Own-loss multiplier for human-wave tactics. Educated guess.

siegeEngineering.note: Attacker power multiplier against fortifications (equivalently a shorter siege) for Roman/Mongol-type engineering. Educated guess.

blitzExploitation.note: Exploitation multiplier for combined-arms armoured breakthroughs; TNDM caps CEV at 1.5 (https://dupuyinstitute.org/2019/12/26/how-attrition-is-calculated-in-the-qjm-vs-the-tndm/). Educated guess.

deepBattleBreakthrough.note: Soviet deep battle echelon breakthrough multiplier. Educated guess.
